correctness.rationale: For three normalized coordinates, L1 distance is twice the infinity norm. Dominating budgets lie in a common coordinate box. At a strictly improved agent, one or two active coordinates all move favorably; a small elementary transfer using active coordinates or a balancing coordinate is box-feasible and strictly improves that agent. The converse is immediate. An exact four-project 5-agent construction exhibits Pareto domination without any elementary transfer. A standalone exact-rational finite test compared independent feasibility and transfer criteria in 49,927 profiles/outcomes, with a separate 12,736-case LP check.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2019 paper proves Pareto optimality of utilitarian budget aggregation and a moving-phantom characterization, not an arbitrary-outcome local certificate. The inspected 2023 portioning paper analyzes axiomatic efficiency and range respect for aggregation rules, but its stated results do not characterize the full Pareto set through single-pair moves. The 2022 three-project mechanism paper targets proportionality and strategic guarantees. Cross-model assignment and convex-optimization results do not imply the L1 simplex theorem. Primary and mathematical-record searches yielded no covering result, although specialist unindexed work remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact O(n)-time public-budget Pareto audit for arbitrary reports and candidate budgets on three natural expenditure categories, rather than only for outcomes of special aggregation rules. The sharp four-project failure reveals a real need for coordinated multiple-coordinate adjustments, clarifying limits of local efficiency certificates.
